finding: Says gains above USD 200 are reported as capital gains (citing Pub. 525). The statute limits the USD 200 exclusion to 'personal transactions' and excludes from that term transactions whose expenses qualify under section 212 (investment). Whether CNY savings held in an interest-bearing deposit are 'personal' or section-212 holdings is fact-dependent; if section 988 applies, gain is ordinary income (988(a)(1)(A)). The capital-gain characterisation should be marked conditional.

Says '>$10,000: customs declaration'. SAFE's own Q&A says amounts above USD 10,000 need a SAFE-issued carry permit and are in principle not allowed except for special destinations; the bank-issued permit covers >5,000–10,000. The deep layer (CH18) states this correctly; the editorial row is inaccurate.
